title: Spell-IT-Out
description: Spell-IT-Out is an EEG dataset recorded from 25 native Italian speakers who listened to sentences, repeated them, and then produced them syllable by syllable at a fixed pace. Production was either overt (spoken aloud) or covert (imagined without movement). The dataset contains 61 EEG channels and 1 EOG channel at 2048 Hz, with hand-corrected word and syllable timing for the overt speech released as events. It supports research on speech production, imagined speech decoding and brain-computer interfaces.
methods_description: EEG was acquired with an ANT Neuro waveguard 64-channel Ag/AgCl cap and an eego sports amplifier at 2048 Hz (reference CPz, ground AFz) in a shielded, acoustically isolated room. Each participant completed 3 overt runs followed by 3 covert runs of 20 sentence trials. Each trial had fixation, listening, repetition and syllabification phases. Overt speech was recorded by microphone, segmented with Silero-VAD, aligned with the Montreal Forced Aligner, and corrected manually in Praat.
